arch_up_edmAccess2023.new_text: GOVERNMENT GUIDE: City of Edmonton, Access Management Guidelines, COE-IM-GUIDE-0023 Version 03, 21 Dec 2023 (J.B. upload 2 Nov 2026): Table 5.10 access width at the property line for commercial, industrial and mixed uses: two-way passenger vehicles 7.5–9.0 m, medium trucks 9.0–11.5 m, large trucks and transit buses 11.5–13.5 m, one-way 5.0 m (6.0 m may be needed for emergency vehicles); 5.6 'For sites with controlled access (e.g., security gates), the access control should be positioned such that at least one vehicle can queue entirely on-site and clear of the public road right-of-way', vehicle length from the largest design vehicle; throat length at least 12 m on collector roads, 6 m on local roads, none on alleys; Table 5.12 minimum throat length, light industrial (our category for a data centre; the table has none) under 10,000 m² site: 15 m (arterial), 40 m (principal roadway); over 10,000 m²: 30 m / 70 m; swept paths with the largest anticipated design vehicle 'may be required' (2.2.2) and are required where widths fall outside Table 5.10/5.11 (5.5). A guideline, not a bylaw. ‖ CHECK 2 (1 Nov 2026, fixed): all widths and throat lengths confirmed; swept-path wording corrected; light-industrial category marked as our reading.
